newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Iran's Aghazadeh says some OPEC members over quota.
newsitem.headline: Iran's Aghazadeh says some OPEC members over quota.

text.p: Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh said an OPEC quota compliance committee meeting found on Wednesday that some OPEC members were pumping above official allocations.
"We feel we have some overproduction and hope members will combat that and adhere to their quotas," Aghazadeh told reporters at the end of the four-man meeting.
Aghazadeh, chairing the committee for the first time, said the quota compliance group would meet again in November ahead of OPEC's next full ministerial conference.
The committee also includes Libya's Abdalla al-Badri and Nigeria's Dan Etete, and was attended by OPEC Secretary General Rilwanu Lukman.
Aghazadeh made no reference to any new methods for monitoring OPEC output or policing overproduction.
He said the committee also looked at supply and demand forecasts for next year.
He said ministers were "satisfied" with oil prices averaging this year more than $2 above 1995.
World demand has easily absorbed the excess in recent months, even at international market prices which on Tuesday were just below five-year highs, at $23 for benchmark Brent crude.
In June OPEC raised its ceiling to 25.03 million barrels per day (bpd) to allow for the eventual resumption of partial Iraqi exports under a U.N. oil-for-food exchange.
But secondary media sources monitored by OPEC put the group's production in August at 25.77 million bpd, despite the postponement of Iraqi sales, OPEC's Secretariat said last week.
